summary: Milestone 2026.05.266 completed with zero experiments in the timing scope: the timing script's look-back window is not anchored to the conductor-state.json activated_at timestamp, so no work is captured regardless of what ran. Both GPUs were idle at 0% utilization with no compute-bound tasks present, making gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks null rather than a flag.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing script look-back window not anchored to conductor-state.json activated_at timestamp — root cause of consecutive empty-timing-window retros; all experiment commits fall outside the captured window.
No post-activation dispatch verification gate: milestone can activate and produce zero artifacts for an entire session with no automated alarm.
No same-session first-dispatch discipline: conductor does not enforce that at least one experiment is launched within N minutes of milestone activation.
improvements_suggested: Fix timing script epoch to use conductor-state.json activated_at field rather than a fixed look-back offset; this single change would populate timing data for every future retro.
Wire a zero-artifact alarm: if no experiment artifact has landed within 60 minutes of milestone activation, emit an automated alert to the outer loop.
Enforce same-session first-dispatch discipline at the conductor level: block milestone activation from completing unless at least one experiment task is queued within the activation turn.

Both GPUs are fully idle (0%, 44C/48C); once the timing fix is deployed, schedule compute-bound experiments to run in parallel across GPU 0 and GPU 1 using DualGPURunner when two or more models are required simultaneously.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix timing epoch to activated_at in scripts/research_conductor.py timing data collection — resolves the root cause of all consecutive empty-timing-window retros in a single code change.

Break pre-test cascade deadlock at outer-loop scope: the task designated to fix the failing pre-test gate was itself blocked by that gate, requiring operator or outer-loop intervention rather than an in-conductor fix.
Wire zero-artifact alarm at 60 minutes post-activation so future empty milestones are caught and escalated within the same session rather than discovered at retro time.
meta_reflection: This is a consecutive empty-timing-window retro with the same root cause that has persisted across many prior milestones: the timing script does not anchor to activated_at. The honest operational finding is not about research throughput but about a structural instrumentation gap — without fixing the timing epoch, retros are informationally empty no matter how much work runs. The highest-leverage action remains unchanged from prior retros: one targeted code change to timing data collection would resolve the information gap for all future milestones.
